items.text: Localization of a scheme at a point
Y=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}\longrightarrow X\ \text{monomorphism, image}=\{x' : x\in\overline{\{x'\}}\}\ \text{(generalizations of }x)
\operatorname{Spec}A_{\mathfrak p}\ni \mathfrak q A_{\mathfrak p}\ \leftrightarrow\ \mathfrak q\subset\mathfrak p
(A_{\mathfrak p})_{\mathfrak qA_{\mathfrak p}}=A_{\mathfrak q}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \mathcal O_{X,x'}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\mathcal O_{Y,x'}
Y=\varprojlim_{U\ni x}U=\bigcap_{U\ni x}U
Local schemes
Local scheme: $Y=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O$, $\mathcal O$ a local ring.
$Y$ local $\iff$ $Y$ quasi-compact with a unique closed point.

Every point of a quasi-compact $Y$ specializes to a closed point (Zorn); unique closed point $a$ $\Rightarrow$ $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{Y,a}\to Y$ surjective, injective, hence a homeomorphism and an isomorphism of locally ringed spaces.
Quasi-compactness is not needed: a scheme with a unique closed point $a$ is $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{Y,a}$.
Morphisms of a local scheme into X
f\colon \operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O\to X\ \longmapsto\ \bigl(x=f(a),\ \ \mathcal O_{X,x}\to\mathcal O\ \text{local}\bigr)
One-to-one correspondence: morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O\to X$ $\leftrightarrow$ pairs (point $x$ of $X$, local homomorphism $\mathcal O_{X,x}\to\mathcal O$).
Affine case: $A\to\mathcal O$ $\leftrightarrow$ the prime $\mathfrak p=\ker(A\to\mathcal O\to\kappa(\mathcal O))$ and a local homomorphism $A_{\mathfrak p}\to\mathcal O$.
\begin{CD} \operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{Y,y} @>>> \operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}\\ @VVV @VVV\\ Y @>{f}>> X \end{CD}
Localization at a point is a functor of the pair $(X,x)$.
Morphisms from the spectrum of a field
\operatorname{Hom}\bigl(\operatorname{Spec}k,\,X\bigr)=\{(x,\ \kappa(x)\hookrightarrow k)\}\qquad \mathcal O_{X,x}\to\kappa(x)\to k
Universal points: $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$, a closed subscheme of $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}$; every $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ factors uniquely through it.
Schemes with one point
$\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O$ reduced to a point $\iff$ $\mathfrak m$ is nil.
$\mathcal O$ noetherian: $\mathfrak m$ nilpotent, $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ of finite type $\Rightarrow$ $\mathcal O$ of finite length (filtration by $\mathfrak m^r$) $\iff$ $\mathcal O$ artinian.
Examples: $k[t]/(t^n)$ (length $n$); $\mathbf Z/p^n\mathbf Z$.
Properties of schemes
Irreducible, connected, quasi-compact; irreducible $\Rightarrow$ connected and non-empty.

Not quasi-compact: the constant group scheme $G_k$ for an infinite set $G$ (infinite disjoint union of open subsets); $\operatorname{Pic}$ of a projective variety over $k$ is an extension of a constant $\mathbf Z$ by a compact group scheme.
Noetherian scheme: quasi-compact, covered by finitely many affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ with $A_i$ noetherian.
\text{equivalently: for every affine open } U,\ \Gamma(U,\mathcal O_X)\ \text{is noetherian}
Locally noetherian: for every affine open $U$, $\Gamma(U)$ noetherian; equivalently every quasi-compact open is noetherian.
Noetherian is not stable: tensor products, $A\otimes_{R}A$ with $A$ the completion of a noetherian local ring are no longer noetherian (descent).
Artinian schemes
$X$ artinian: $X\simeq\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A$ artinian (finite length as a module; descending chain condition on ideals).

Artinian $\iff$ noetherian and discrete (hence finite): $A=\prod_i A_{x_i}$, a product of local Artin rings $\mathcal O_{x_i}$ with $\mathfrak m_i$ nilpotent, finite-dimensional over the residue field.
A noetherian scheme with finitely many points need not be artinian (example: $V$ a discrete valuation ring).
